newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker RGI profits fall but sees progress.
newsitem.headline: Aker RGI profits fall but sees progress.

text.p: Norwegian industrial holding group Aker RGI ASA on Tuesday reported profits after financial items for the full year 1996 of 969 million crowns ($142 million), down from 1.31 billion crowns a year earlier.
The company attributed the 26 percent decline primarily to an extraordinary pre-tax gain of 543 million crowns in 1995 from Aker subsidiary Norwegian Contractors, which has been wound up.
Aker RGI said operating profits for the 12-month period amounted to 421 million crowns versus 1.24 billion crowns. Consolidated revenues were 20.41 billion against 17.05 billion.

The comparative 1995 figures were calculated on a pro forma basis following the establishment of the conglomerate last year from the merger of engineering and construction company Aker ASA and investment group Resource Group International ASA (RGI).
"Most of the companies in which Norway's Aker RGI group is involved reported progress for 1996," the company said in a statement.

The group's core business areas are Nordic cement and building materials group Scancem, fishing and fish processing company Norway Seafoods -- the world's largest operator for catching and processing white fish -- and the offshore services firm Aker Maritime.
